mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month indicates a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with deflationary pressure, which historically has been associated with negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than -0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises above its 12-month moving average by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is a contradictory signal indicating labor market churning; this ambiguity typically precedes equity market volatility, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE and PAYEMS rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which typically precedes a consumer spending slowdown and ultimately reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.
